A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASTGI research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison; rendered figures resolve extraction difficulties.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments on four datasets, component ablations, parameter sensitivity studies, and learned-graph and embedding visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Table 2, Tables 3–4, Figure 4, and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The encoders, nearest-neighbor construction, causal masking, message passing, query prediction, and MSE objective are unchanged. v3 explicitly states that coordinates and topology remain fixed during propagation; this clarifies the existing equations rather than establishing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate forecasting on MIMIC, PhysioNet, Human Activity, and USHCN with the same represented populations and domains. v3 Table 1 summarizes these retained datasets; Appendix B.1 confirms unchanged coverage.

E2.justification: The same twelve baselines participate in v2 Table 1 and v3 Table 2, with unchanged adaptations in Appendix B.2. The expanded citations do not introduce additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The 80/10/10 splits, preprocessing descriptions, MSE/MAE metrics, AdamW optimization, 300-epoch limit, and five-epoch early stopping remain unchanged. Newly supplied dataset descriptors do not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: Both retain the same four component ablations, sensitivity studies for K, L, channel dimension and hidden dimension, and MIMIC case studies in Appendices C–D. Splitting and relocating the ablation table adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 removes the explicit seed values 2024–2028. Both versions still report five independent seeds and mean ± standard deviation; there is no stated change in run count or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All matched forecasting and ablation scores are identical. Figure 4 retains the same sensitivity results, and Figures 5–6 retain the same qualitative findings. v2 Table 2 is redistributed into v3 Tables 3–4 without numerical changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propagation equations, prediction equations, and loss remain equivalent. v3 numbers previously unnumbered problem definitions and reformats equations; it adds no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about avoiding representation distortion, learning adaptive interactions, and outperforming existing methods. Replacing some uses of 'regression' with 'forecasting' does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 3.4 explicitly distinguish fixed positional anchors and topology from evolving feature-dependent interaction weights. Section 4.1 also explains benchmark breadth through dimensionality and sampling density. Existing performance interpretations and overfitting/oversmoothing cautions remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds code/data access information and a reproducibility statement. Table 1 newly supplies maximum sequence lengths and average observation counts while repeating sample and variable counts from Appendix B.1. Exact seed identifiers are removed. Repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially expand the cited literature to additional forecasting surveys and benchmarks, graph/hypergraph studies, and broad NLP, vision, image-editing and video-generation work. This broadens the reference scope considerably, although the two-paradigm taxonomy and central novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: v3 adds localized explanations, acknowledgements and a reproducibility statement, updates author/header information, and swaps the sensitivity and ablation subsections. Most scientific prose and all appendix explanations remain unchanged; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds a dataset summary table and splits the dense combined ablation table into more readable MSE and MAE tables. It moves table captions above the tables, clarifies Figure 1's caption, cleans up Figure 3, and shortens Figure 4's parameter labels. Appendix figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through the fixed-topology explanation, additional dataset descriptors, and more readable ablation tables. New code/data access information also improves documented reproducibility, although availability is unverified. These gains outweigh the limited loss of exact seed information and reduced focus from broad citation additions. The underlying scientific claims and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
